court: High Court of Judicature at Bombay
trial_court: Family Court, Mumbai at Bandra (MJ Petition No.C-4 of 2013)
case_name: Mrs. Amee Sharan Desai vs Mr. Sharan Sanjeev Desai
acts_cited_auto: Protection of Women from DV Act, 2005

acts_cited.act: Protection of Women from DV Act, 2005

facts_of_case: Petitioner-wife claimed interim maintenance for herself and minor daughter; trial court refused maintenance to wife but granted Rs.15,000/- per month to daughter.

legal_principles.principle: The concept of sustenance does not necessarily mean to lead the life of an animal, feel like an unperson to be thrown away from grace and roam for her basic maintenance somewhere else.
legal_principles.held: She is entitled in law to lead a life in the similar manner as she would have lived in the house of her husband.
cited_cases: Bhuwan Mohan Singh v. Meena, (2015) 6 SCC 353
legal_principles.significance: HIGH — to ensure a dignified life for the wife

legal_principles.principle: The husband cannot take subterfuges to deprive her of the benefit of living with dignity.
legal_principles.held: In a proceeding of this nature, the husband cannot take subterfuges to deprive her of the benefit of living with dignity.
cited_cases: Bhuwan Mohan Singh v. Meena, (2015) 6 SCC 353
legal_principles.significance: HIGH — to prevent exploitation of the wife

legal_principles.principle: It is the sacrosanct duty to render financial support even if the husband is required to earn money with physical labour, if he is able-bodied.
legal_principles.held: A situation is not to be maladroitly created whereunder she is compelled to resign to her fate and think of life 'dust unto dust'.
cited_cases: Bhuwan Mohan Singh v. Meena, (2015) 6 SCC 353
legal_principles.significance: HIGH — to ensure the wife's basic needs are met

outcome.final_order: Interim maintenance of Rs.2,50,000/- per month for the Petitioner-wife and Rs.1,50,000/- per month for the minor daughter is granted.
